question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay that can override mutable config and block weakening writes, or keep enterprise policy in conformance-only Policy/Nix-managed config surfaces?
rationale: The request changes config precedence, runtime write behavior, diagnostics, and the security boundary between core config, Policy conformance, and operator-managed deployment files; current main only implements adjacent conformance and Nix immutability pieces.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hook design settles
options.body: Leave the issue open while related policy-hook proposals clarify whether enforcement should live in plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue, authored the prior exact implementation candidate, and is the clearest routing owner for the security-boundary decision.
